neighbours.label: ' in' after a classifying adjective in the frame '<adjective> in nature / character / scope' ('animistic in nature'); more weakly other function words right after a term that is being characterised
fire: The dispute was largely political in nature, and the courts refused to hear it.
Their early paintings are abstract in character and rarely show human figures.
The council's powers are advisory in nature, so its votes bind nobody.
Most of these tremors are volcanic in origin and cause little damage.
The new tax is regressive in effect, falling hardest on the poor.
Her later novels are autobiographical in nature and draw on her childhood.
The society was monastic in character, with strict rules on silence.
The agreement is provisional in nature and may be revised next year.
quiet: The dispute was heard in March, and the courts refused to settle it.
Their early paintings hang in Vienna and rarely leave the museum.
The council's members meet in private, so its votes surprise nobody.
Most of these tremors occur in winter and cause little damage.
The new tax arrives in April, falling hardest on the poor.
Her later novels were written in exile and draw on her childhood.
The society gathered in silence, with strict rules on speech.
The agreement was signed in haste and may be revised next year.

notes: Top examples peak on function words (with, in, of, or, be, usually, often) just after a technical term being described; no single token. Probes were weak: 'bilateral in nature' 0.24, 'polytheistic in character' 0.25, 'exothermic in nature' 0.24, 'is often caused' 0.22, 'is usually defined' 0.23, but 'traditionally defined' 0.02 and 'sometimes triggered' 0.05. Only the 'in nature' frame was consistent, at about the judge's 0.20 threshold, so this is a narrow sub-trigger and may fail on the median; near misses keep ' in' after a verb.
